pages.text: Each process gets a number, its $(l)PID$(). When it starts, a dark PID block appears on the cursor rail at line 0. Its height is the PID: the first free spot counted up from y=0.

The PID block shows the PID in green on its north and south faces. Its east and west faces show where the trigger block stands.$(br2)Several processes of one program can run at the same time, one per trigger block. Each has its own PID block and its own cursor. They don't share any variables.
